corrections.text: The summary says InfoQ's November 14 report 'names only 26.10.0'. That holds for the three features in the headline (util.debounce, util.throttle and crypto.parsePKCS12), which InfoQ places in 26.10.0 and never ties to Node.js 24. The InfoQ article also names Node.js 26.11.0, as the release that 'followed with further Buffer and http helpers', as the article's body notes.
